title: A Pensioner Hid Cocaine in His Mobility Scooter
central_question: Ronald Lord, 71, flew into Gatwick from Barbados in February 2025; Border Force X-rayed his mobility scooter and found about 8 kg of cocaine behind the seat back. He said he'd had a week in Barbados (the airline said three days) and that he had no idea how it got there (the panel's screw was in his pocket). He pleaded guilty and was jailed for six years. What gave him away: the screw or the three days?
content_notes: Tone: dry and ironic; the joke is on the scheme (a story of a week that was three days, and a panel whose screw was in his pocket), never on age or disability. Ronald Lord pleaded guilty and was sentenced (Croydon Crown Court, Aug and Sept 2025) and is named by the NCA and the press, so he is named; he is drawn ONLY as a dark rim-lit silhouette (NOT A LIKENESS), seated at an interview desk and standing in a dock. Nothing reported says whether he needs the scooter: no line or picture implies he faked it, and he is never shown walking away from it. The scooter is a generic red mobility scooter (colour and model not reported); the packages are plain wrapped blocks. The Border Force officer and the judge are generic figures with no badge, patch, crest, flag, agency name or insignia; no weapon; no force. The search bay, interview room and court are illustrations, not reported places; no airline, airport sign or logo is copied. The travel record is our own typed graphic, not a boarding pass or any real document. The NCA wording on the fun-fact card is attributed and carried by the NCA release and relayed by several outlets. No dialogue is invented. The CBC-only report of 'work trip' messages is not used. Facts verified 2026-10-25.

lines.text: A pensioner hid cocaine in his mobility scooter.
8 kilos of cocaine sat behind the seat.
Then Border Force X-rayed the scooter.
He said he'd had a week in Barbados.
But the airline said three days.
He claimed he had no idea.
Investigators said he thought a pensioner would be less of a target.
The panel's screw was in his pocket.

claims.text: A 71-year-old pensioner (the NCA's word) was stopped at Gatwick on 7 February 2025 with cocaine hidden in a void in the seat-back panel of his mobility scooter. He pleaded guilty. Narration: 'A pensioner hid cocaine in his mobility scooter.' Headline 'A MOBILITY SCOOTER / WITH 8 KG INSIDE'. The plea establishes knowing importation; the reel does not say who built the void.

About 8 kg (18 lb) of cocaine was in the void behind the seat-back panel. Narration: '8 kilos of cocaine sat behind the seat.' Label 'GATWICK AIRPORT · 7 FEB 2025'. The value (about £640,000, NCA) is not narrated.

Border Force officers X-rayed the mobility scooter and found the cocaine in a hidden void in the seat back panel. Narration (gotcha): 'Then Border Force X-rayed the scooter.' Callout '8 KG BEHIND THE SEAT BACK'. The scooter's colour, model and the wrapping are not reported: drawn generic.
He had flown into London Gatwick from Barbados and was stopped by Border Force on 7 February 2025. Label 'GATWICK AIRPORT · 7 FEB 2025', sub 'Flight from Barbados · Border Force'.

He is Ronald Lord, 71, from Montreal (CBC: a Chateauguay address, a Montreal suburb); he pleaded guilty and is named by the NCA and widely in the press. Narration: 'Ronald Lord. 71. From Montreal.' Label 'RONALD LORD · 71 · MONTREAL', sub 'Pleaded guilty · NOT A LIKENESS'. Drawn only as a silhouette.
He told officers he was coming to the UK to sightsee after a seven-day holiday in Barbados. Narration (re-hook): 'He said he'd had a week in Barbados.'

Checks with airlines showed he had spent only three days in Barbados. Narration: 'But the airline said three days.' Evidence close-up (our own typed travel-record graphic, no real document imitated): 'HE SAID: 7 DAYS' struck through, 'AIRLINE CHECKS: 3 DAYS' circled.
He denied knowing about the drugs and said he did not know how they got into the scooter. Narration: 'He claimed he had no idea.' Label 'HE SAID: NO IDEA HOW IT GOT IN'.

Attributed wording from the NCA's statement (carried by the NCA release and relayed by Global News, Yahoo and The Nightly): NCA senior investigating officer Richard Wickham said he obviously thought that because he was a pensioner he would be 'less of a target for law enforcement'. Narration: 'Investigators said he thought a pensioner would be less of a target.' Label 'THE NCA: "LESS OF A TARGET"', sub 'Senior investigating officer'.
FUN FACT: he told officers he was coming to the UK to go sightseeing (after what he said was a seven-day holiday in Barbados). Card 'HE SAID HE'D COME TO THE UK / TO GO SIGHTSEEING'.
He pleaded guilty to class A drug smuggling at Croydon Crown Court on 5 August 2025. Narration: 'He pleaded guilty.' Label 'CROYDON CROWN COURT', sub 'Pleaded guilty · jailed Sept 2025'.
STATISTIC (counter 6 YEARS): he was sentenced to six years in prison at Croydon Crown Court on 5 September 2025. Narration: 'Six years.'

When he was searched, a screw from the scooter's seat panel was found in his pocket. Narration (callback): 'The panel's screw was in his pocket.' Callout on the empty screw hole 'THE SCREW FROM THIS PANEL', sub 'Found in his pocket'.
